pr_title: Fix flashlight not dimming if slider head is hit early
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/ppy/osu/issues/26551

\>_<

Fix is a bit nuclear (`OnUpdate` should be considered last resort), but I don't see many better alternatives here as `ApplyCustomUpdateState` does not work...

issue_context.title: Flashlight dim is not always applied to sliders
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

I noticed that the flashlight dim is not always triggered on sliders. It seems to be random since not always the same sliders that trigger / don't trigger the dim. I tried with and without modifying the mod settings but the same random behavior is observed.

### Screenshots or videos

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SGs0W2WBJR8
Notice that the dim is applied to the very first slider and not applied for the following ~20 sliders.

### Version

2024.114.0

### Logs

[compressed-logs.zip](https://github.com/ppy/osu/files/13943092/compressed-logs.zip)

review_comments: I'd rather not. The current solution may be nuclear but at least it's simple.

I'm not sure I agree? Making it run every single update frame for every single slider is way too hacky for me compared to just making the thing run when it's supposed to run? You might also be able to get it working with `BeginAbsoluteSequence` and transform `FlashlightDim` instead of scheduling, but I don't see the point in `OnUpdate` to be honest.
Disregarding performance concerns, there's NO WAY a scheduler's `AddDelayed` will work as you expect it to. It won't handle rewind or pause or anything.

It will...it's part of `DrawableRuleset`'s frame stability container. It's timed alongside every single gameplay component there (i.e. `Flashlight.Clock = FrameStableClock`).

And regarding performance concerns, this method fires off whenever a slider changes its tracking state. I'm not an expert when it comes to delegate memory footprint or whatever other performance concerns that comes, but if such callback qualifies as bad for scheduling, then sure...`OnUpdate` I guess.
I continue to think that while the current solution may be a touch primitive it is still better (in being less prone to failure) than any of the proposed alternatives.
I'll take back my proposal of using schedulers because of the potential performance concerns from delegate allocations and what not.

> It will...it's part of DrawableRuleset's frame stability container. It's timed alongside every single gameplay component there (i.e. Flashlight.Clock = FrameStableClock).

I have zero faith in this. `Scheduler` was never made to account for time going backwards, seeking, or anything else. There is zero chance it will not break *something*.
